structured_output.what_is_happening: DotFomo is a Pump.fun token that migrated to PumpSwap about 21 seconds after it was created, so it was almost certainly bundled or sniped at launch. About 35 minutes after the pool opened, it had risen roughly 180–1,800% (depending on the source) to about $133–137k market cap. It had about $31k of burned LP liquidity, about $170k of volume, and around 950 unique buyers against 700 sellers. At detection it was at or near its all-time high of $0.000139. It has a website (dotfomo.com), an X account (@dotfomo_) and a DexScreener profile, with no paid boosts or ads.

narrative.description: The name 'DotFomo' reads like a brand or product launch (a .com site plus a dedicated X account), possibly a FOMO or trading-app meta. The packet has no description, so the actual story is unknown.
narrative.why_spreading: The activity looks like launch-momentum trading: high turnover (5.3x liquidity per hour), a large number of bundler and sniper wallets, and some smart/KOL wallets. There is no evidence of organic social spread beyond the project's own links, and GMGN shows only 71 page visits.

token_connection.why_this_token: This is the earliest pair (created before all the copycats), and it is the only one with real liquidity. It links to the project's website and X account and has the DexScreener profile.
token_connection.competing_tokens: Four same-name copycats were created after it. All are low-cap, and three have zero liquidity. They pose no real threat.

authenticity.evidence: Signs of a coordinated launch: migration 21 seconds after creation, 79 bundler wallets, 38 snipers, 27 graph-detected insiders across several transfer networks, and a 37% bot/degen rate. The dev account has launched other tokens (2 by the creator wallet, 5 by the linked X account). On the other side: the dev holds only 0.08%, top-10 holders own 27.6% (excluding the pool), and there are about 950 unique buyers, 13 smart wallets and 3 renowned wallets. The LP is burned and there is no paid promotion.
authenticity.uncertainty: There is no X post data, so we can't tell whether any real community or KOL is pushing it. Most of the supply held by the insider networks may already have been sold into the pump.

structural_risks: A bundled, near-instant migration means insider supply can dump into late buyers
Entry would be at or near a parabolic ATH after a roughly 18x move in 30 minutes
The insider transfer networks (27 wallets) look like a coordinated distribution setup
Liquidity of about $31k is thin relative to the volume, so slippage is high and a crash would be fast
The dev's X account has launched several tokens (serial launcher)

structured_output.counterargument: It is the canonical token, has a real-looking brand (website plus X), burned LP, low dev holdings, and fairly spread-out top holders. Smart and KOL wallets are involved, and buyers still outnumber sellers in the last 5 minutes. Tokens like this sometimes run from about $130k to $300–500k in the first hour or two once KOLs post about them, and the burned LP rules out a classic liquidity pull.
unknowns: What DotFomo actually is, and whether the website or product is real
The X account's follower count and whether KOLs are posting about it
How much of the bundled supply has already been sold
The price path during the 25 minutes before entry

source_coverage.notes: This was the offline condition, so only the evidence packet was used.

structured_output.thesis: This is a bundled, fast-migrated launch that has pumped hard and is at its ATH at detection. Entry comes 25 minutes later, most likely after the move is exhausted, so the stop at -50% is more likely to be hit than a further 2x. Burned LP rules out a literal liquidity pull, but a dump that effectively kills the pair is quite possible. Its canonical status and some smart-money interest keep a real runner chance alive, but it is still below the 1/3 break-even.
